lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn helps students recognise and understand where ‘can’ and ‘can’t’ are used within sentence structures, preparing them for writing and speaking activities.
Look for understanding of the grammar shown in the table and evidence of understanding key structures.
“We’re going on an activity day. I need to know what you can and can’t do! If you can cook, you can make lunch!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - B. Look and write

details: Look and write develops writing and comprehension by helping students practise positive and negative sentences. Students complete the sentences using the picture prompts,  reinforcing key vocabulary.
Look for neat handwriting, accurate spelling and students using the picture cues carefully.
“These friends have drawn pictures to tell me what they can and can;t do. Can you write the words for them?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - A Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking beginning-sound recognition. Students listen for the target word, match its first sound to the correct letter choice and show understanding by neatly circling the right option.
Look for careful listening, mostly accurate letter choices, clear circling and steady pencil control,
“What can you see on this page? Listen carefully, and help me find the correct starting sound for each word. Then let’s say each word together.”

Heads Down:

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - A Point and say

details: Point and say reviews key vocabulary in the pictures. Students link spoken words to the visual items and practice clear pronunciation through short, supported repetition.
Look for correct pointing, clear word repetition and most students confidently saying the target vocabulary.
“Amazing word! Time to use our English skills one more time. What animal words can you find in this story?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - B Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops students’ ability to connect spoken language with written text. It helps them build confidence in reading along with audio support.
Look for careful listening, accurate recognition of key vocabulary and appropriate intonation when reading aloud.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - C How many words start with a y? How many words end with an x?

details: How many words start with a y? How many words end with an x helps students to focus on the key initial and ending sounds of words and helps with counting accuracy.
Look for correct counting of the words with the target initial and ending sounds and accurate recognition of target letters.
“You can now recognise all the alphabet! What words can you find starting with y? What words end with x?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - D Circle the words that start with y and end with an x

details: Circle words that start with y and end with an x develops students’ ability to recognise initial and ending sounds in print. Students scan the speech bubbles and captions, identify the correct letters, and show understanding by circling the correct words.
Look for accurate identification of y– and x words, neat circling and steady pencil control.
